title: Learn to do (Avot 4:5)
hookLine: learn in order to teach, and learn in order to do
tomorrow: what's wrong with using what you know to get ahead?

cards: Somewhere there's a folder of saved posts, recipes, workouts and how-to clips that will never be opened again. Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka, answers that folder.
Whoever learns in order to teach is given the means to learn and to teach. Whoever learns in order to do is given the means to learn, to teach, to keep and to do.

teach.b: Look at the two lists. Learning in order to teach is given learning and teaching.

Learning in order to do is given those, plus keeping and doing. Doing doesn't skip the learning or the teaching; it's the bigger box with both inside. Notice the words al menat, in order to: the saying cares about aim.
Two people can sit over the same page, and the one who means to do something with it walks away with more.
That's Chanina ben Dosa's deeds first, back in chapter three, now as a promise: learning lands when it moves your hands.
So what does this give you this week? A filter.
Of everything you're taking in, ask which piece you'll actually use by the weekend, and learn that one well enough to do it. The rest isn't wasted. It's just still in the folder.

how: Jewish study is traditionally tied to practice; some learners finish a session by choosing one thing from it to keep that week.

o: study aimed at doing, which brings more with it
studying only so you can teach a class one day
following the rules first and studying them later

games.q: the two lists — tap the pairs.

s: in this saying, learning in order to teach is the highest aim
learning in order to do is given more: to learn, teach, keep and do.
the saying treats doing as a reason to skip study
doing includes the learning; it doesn't replace it.
whoever learns in order to do is given the means to teach as well

games.q: you finished a budgeting course and loved every lesson. your bank account looks exactly the same. the saying suggests:
o: pick one step from the course and do it this week.
sign up for the advanced course; more learning will fix it.
teach the course to a friend, and count that as enough.
games.why: learning to teach is given learning and teaching; learning to do is given those, and keeping and doing too.

practice: Bring to mind one thing you learned recently and haven't used yet: a skill, a kindness, a fact. Name where you could do it in the next day, and the one thing most likely to stop you.
Then decide what you'll do when that obstacle shows up.

wordCard.voice: Learn to do. Halomed al menat la'asot: study aimed at the hands, which is given learning, teaching, keeping and doing.

orig.note: Hebrew: whoever learns in order to do, the larger aim in Avot 4:5.

carryVoice: The line: learn to do, and the doing brings the rest along with it. Lehitraot, until we meet again.

sources.ref: Mishnah Avot 4:5 (Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka)
Mishnah Avot 3:9 (Chanina ben Dosa: deeds exceeding wisdom)
